top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a specific, separable and mature achievement: the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, which lets many neutral atoms be interrogated without a light-shift penalty and has been taken to the 10^-18 level, reproduced and surpassed by independent laboratories, and applied to redshift tests and dark-matter and varying-constant bounds. The allocation to Katori (concept and realisation) and Ye (many-body and comb-linked development) is clean, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock and not to precision metrology generally. P002 is a genuine and mature discovery but has only one explicit supporter and a three-way allocation that is contested; a prize is still preferable to none, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: Field proximity only: Kroll is an atomic physicist who spent time in John Hall's laboratory, and Hall's group is the lineage of Jun Ye's work; no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye is apparent from the profile.
